summary: Two external IPs password-sprayed university accounts before authenticating as b.cetin@aegean.edu (F2,F3). The account appeared in a Markovian spray roster from 78.187.4.44 across 10 time windows (F4). Authentication occurred from previously unseen device PH-9900 instead of the usual LT-6002 (F1). Risk Gate escalates to contain despite unconfirmed signals.

actions.action: Force password reset and revoke all active sessions for b.cetin@aegean.edu; inspect sign-in logs for devices PH-9900 and LT-6002.
Enforce account lockout and MFA; block IPs 78.187.4.44 and 193.140.10.17 at the perimeter.
Hunt for additional successful authentications from the two IPs and unseen devices across the tenant.

limitations: Confidence is moderate because findings are unconfirmed signals only; no endpoint or mailbox evidence has been reviewed.

not_checked: Endpoint telemetry on PH-9900, mailbox access rules, and lateral movement from the compromised session were not checked.

risk.rationale: Confirmed account takeover chain: two distinct external IPs (78.187.4.44 and 193.140.10.17) each performed password spraying against 56-67 accounts and subsequently authenticated successfully as b.cetin@aegean.edu (T1110.003 + T1078), likelihood 0.85 each. The account also appears in the password-spray roster from 78.187.4.44 (likelihood 0.7), and the successful sign-in occurred from a previously unseen device PH-9900 versus the usual LT-6002 (likelihood 0.6). Multiple independent spray-then-success chains against the same user constitute a confirmed compromise, not merely weak or explained signals. No conflicting or insufficient evidence requiring human escalation.
escalate_reasons: model proposed contain, evidence policy says monitor
